P-17-geografiya.текст: Ultra-premium cinematic editorial frame, vertical 4:5 aspect ratio, exactly 1080 by 1350 pixels, four to five ratio locked and never changed, built as slide one, the cover, of a five-slide Instagram carousel about the geography of a Moscow production site, composed like the cover of a serious business magazine and never like a presentation slide or an advertising poster. The scene is a heavy engineering drafting table photographed straight down from directly above, camera axis exactly perpendicular to the table top, zero lens tilt, no converging lines, no wide angle distortion, deep depth of field edge to edge. Filling the frame is one large brushed steel plate laid on the dark table, its surface honestly worn with fine circular machining marks, scuffs, a chipped corner and oxidised hex bolts at the four corners, and into that plate is deep machine-engraved a schematic map of the south of Moscow: the Moscow ring road drawn as one closed engraved ring cut wide and deep, the inner ring of the third transport ring drawn as a second smaller closed ring above it, the river cut as a wide meandering channel, the street grid reduced to fine hairline grooves, and two principal radial highways engraved as the widest channels of all, running from the lower area of the plate up and inwards, crossing the ring road and continuing toward the inner ring. The map is abstract, technical and monochrome, a machined engineering document and not an atlas, with no country outlines, no compass rose, no scale bar and no minute markings. At the point where the two radial highways sit inside the ring, a single machined amber marker is inlaid flush into the steel: a small solid circle of amber with a thin concentric ring around it, the one warmest and brightest point in the whole picture, connected by a hairline leader rule one to two pixels thick to the address line below it, and thin engraved sight lines radiate from that marker out along the two highways to the ring, so the eye reads immediately that the point sits inside the ring and feeds two exits. Every inscription is engraved into the steel plate itself and never laid on top of the image. The map labels are deep-engraved in a dense condensed technical sans with wide letter tracking, each on one unbroken line, each set along or beside the line it names and always upright, never rotated to unreadable angles, at a capital height of about one and eight tenths percent of the frame height, reading exactly «МКАД» placed on the outer ring, «ТТК» placed on the inner ring, «Каширское шоссе» placed beside the right-hand radial highway and «Варшавское шоссе» placed beside the left-hand radial highway. The headline occupies the upper third of the plate on three left-aligned lines with no hyphenation, deep-engraved into a slightly raised milled panel of the same steel so the letters sit in their own shallow field, set in the same dense condensed sans with wide tracking, and it reads exactly, line one «ДАЛЕКО» СЧИТАЕТСЯ where the single word ДАЛЕКО is wrapped in Russian guillemet quotation marks, line two В МИНУТАХ, line three И В ОТГРУЗКАХ, each line at a capital height of about seven and a half percent of the frame height with leading equal to one and one tenth capital heights, all three sharing one left margin, and this three-line headline is the single largest and most dominant element in the whole image. Beneath the headline, separated by a clear gap equal to one headline capital height and underlined by one hairline engraved rule that runs the width of the headline block, a single unbroken line reads exactly «Юг Москвы, внутри МКАД, 6-я Радиальная, 17с1» at a capital height of about two and four tenths percent of the frame height, left aligned to the same margin, and the digits inside this address line are the only digits anywhere in the frame. There are no minutes, no travel times, no kilometre figures, no percentages and no other numerals of any kind in the picture. Geometry is strict: an eight column grid with six percent outer margins, the headline block occupying columns one to six of the upper third, the engraved map filling the lower two thirds, the amber marker sitting near the optical centre of the map, and a guaranteed clear space of at least three percent of the frame height around every piece of type so that no letter is crossed by a road groove, a leader rule, a bolt or the frame edge. The palette is locked to five hexadecimal values and nothing else exists anywhere in the picture, including reflections, glints, rust, dust and spill light: amber #E8A400 as the one and only accent, used for the site marker, the sight lines and the light caught in the deepest engraved grooves; muted gold #C9A233 for secondary reflections on the brushed steel and the bolt heads; graphite #14171C for the steel plate body and the machined surface; ink black #0E1116 for the table around the plate, the deep engraved shadow and the falloff at the frame corners; warm white #F5F1E8 for the lit crests of the engraving, hairline rules and all lettering. No blue, no green, no red, no cyan, no magenta, no teal, no purple, no neon, no cyberpunk glow, no map colour coding, no colour grading and no colour cast outside these five values. Lighting is architectural and cinematic: one hard directional amber key enters from the upper left at a raking thirty five degree angle so every engraved groove, milled edge and bolt head throws a long soft-edged shadow down and to the right and the lettering reads by relief alone, one weak muted gold bounce from the lower right just lifts the deepest shadow, and ink black falloff swallows the lower right corner, with no second light source, no practical lamps inside the frame and no lens flare. Fine film grain, no vignetting, no bokeh balls, no HDR halos, no glossy varnish. Absolutely no additional text, no captions, no subtitles, no extra numbers, no minutes, no street names beyond the four specified, no north arrow, no watermarks, no logos, no invented words, no Latin transliteration and no gibberish letterforms; only the nine inscriptions specified here, reproduced character by character with exact Cyrillic spelling, exact guillemet quotation marks, exact digits, exact punctuation and exact spacing. The three-line headline must remain perfectly legible when the whole frame is scaled down to a feed thumbnail about three hundred pixels wide: keep it high contrast warm white on near black, unobstructed, and never let a road groove, leader rule, bolt or shadow cut across its letterforms. No drawn interface elements: no call-to-action buttons, button shapes with text, swipe-up arrows, link chips, cursors, app icons or screen mock-ups; every word lives on a real surface.
